cards.front: What should you know about key sequence?
cards.back: Air travels through the respiratory system in this exact order: Nose → Pharynx → Larynx → Trachea → Bronchi → Bronchioles → Alveoli

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Cardio-Respiratory System
cards.back: Gaseous exchange is the diffusion of gases between the alveoli and the blood in the surrounding capillaries. Oxygen moves from the alveoli into the blood, and carbon dioxide moves from the blood into the alveoli.

cards.front: What should you know about features that make alveoli efficient for gaseous exchange?
cards.back: Large surface area - approximately 70m² (roughly the size of a tennis court) Thin walls - alveoli and capillary walls are each one cell thick, creating a very short diffusion distance Moist lining - gases dissolve in the moisture before diffusing Dense capillary network - ensures constant blood flow for efficient exchange Good ventilation - constant supply of fresh air maintains the concentration gradient

cards.front: What should you know about the heart?
cards.back: is a muscular pump with four chambers : two atria (upper, receiving chambers) and two ventricles (lower, pumping chambers). It is divided into a right side (pumping deoxygenated blood to the lungs) and a left side (pumping oxygenated blood to the body).

cards.front: What should you know about why the left ventricle has the thickest wall?
cards.back: The left ventricle must pump blood to the entire body (systemic circulation), requiring much higher pressure than the right ventricle, which only pumps blood to the nearby lungs (pulmonary circulation).

cards.front: What should you know about key concept?
cards.back: Humans have a double circulatory system - blood passes through the heart twice for each complete circuit of the body. This allows blood to be pumped at a much higher pressure, delivering oxygen more efficiently.

cards.front: What should you know about capillary adaptation for exchange?
cards.back: Capillary walls are only one cell thick , creating a very short diffusion distance. This allows oxygen, carbon dioxide, glucose and waste products to diffuse efficiently between the blood and body tissues.

cards.back: 1. For The Cardio-Respiratory System questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question
Two nasal passages with hairs and mucous membrane (e.g. Filters dust and bacteria; warms and moistens the air)
Muscular tube shared with digestive system (e.g. Passageway for air to the larynx)
Contains vocal cords; epiglottis on top (e.g. Epiglottis prevents food entering the trachea; produces sound)
Tube with C-shaped cartilage rings; lined with cilia and mucus (e.g. Carries air to the bronchi; cartilage prevents collapse; cilia move mucus and trapped particles upward)
Two branches (left and right) from the trachea (e.g. Carry air into each lung; also lined with cartilage and cilia)
Smaller branches within each lung (e.g. Distribute air throughout the lungs; smooth muscle controls diameter)
Tiny air sacs at the end of bronchioles; surrounded by capillaries (e.g. Site of gaseous exchange between air and blood)
